headline: Approved July 21 minutes and adopted Findings & Decisions for Grandview Avenue; discussed chicken-keeping policy options
summary: The board approved the July 21, 2026 minutes as amended and adopted the Findings & Decisions for Grandview Avenue. Staff presented options for regulating chicken keeping in response to a new state law, discussed signing an old Fairways subdivision plan from 2018, and gave an update on Land Use Plan consultant review.
decisions: Approved the minutes of July 21, 2026 as amended.
Adopted the Findings & Decisions for Grandview Avenue.

MEETING MINUTES 
 
                   Board Members Present:  Chair Jonathan Boucher (via Zoom) 
Vice Chair Janet Jonas (Acting Chair) 
Ted Brush 
Trisha Hayes 
Greg Hobson 
Ken Huhn (via Zoom) 
Ross Whitford 
 
      
City Staff Present:   Anja Collette, Planning Officer  
        Matt Altiero, Planning Analyst 
Grace Innis, Assistant City Solicitor 
 
 
Vice Chair Jonas called the meeting to order at 7:00 P.M.  
 
OLD BUSINESS 
1. Meeting Minutes – July 21, 2026 
Member Hobson moved to approve the minutes of July 21, 2026 as amended. Seconded by Member Brush. 
Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
2. Adoption of Findings & Decisions for Grandview Avenue  
 
Member Brush moved that the Board adopt the Findings & Decisions for Grandview Avenue. Seconded by 
Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – all voting members in favor, none opposed. Motion passed. 
OTHER BUSINESS 
1. Chickens Discussion 
 
Vice Chair Jonas introduced the agenda item. 
 
Planning Officer Collette provided an overview, describing the policy question of how to address chicken 
keeping. She discussed a new state law that prevents municipalities from prohibiting chicken keeping in 
residential zones. Collette explained options such as setting a minimum lot size, creating setbacks, and limiting

the number of hens based on lot size. She provided the recommendation that multi-unit buildings require 
landlord and all tenant approval. Collette discussed efforts to prevent vermin. 
 
Chair Boucher asked about requirements for registering – Planning Officer Collette responded chicken coops 
would require a Certificate of Occupancy, which would include an inspection from Code Enforcement and 
Animal Control. 
 
Vice Chair Jonas asked if chicken coops would require building permits – Planning Officer Collette clarified 
they would not.  
 
Vice Chair Jonas provided positive feedback to the preventative provisions towards predators and vermin. She 
commented that many coops are heated in the winter, recommending the inclusion of language such as 
“ensure proper use to prevent fires.” Jonas expressed that no roosters should be allowed. Planning Officer 
Collette responded that if electrical service is connected to a coop, it must meet the National Electrical Code. 
 
Chair Boucher asked about different types of domestic birds, such as ducks or quails – Planning Officer 
Collette responded they would remain limited to lots in the Rural Residence and Agricultural District of at least 
one and a half acres. 
 
Vice Chair Jonas asked for additional comments – there were none. 
 
2. Signing of Old Subdivision Plan for Fairways 
 
Vice Chair Jonas introduced the agenda item, explaining that a subdivision plan passed in 2018 needed to be 
signed and recorded.  
 
3. Follow-Up/ Thoughts on Land Use Plan Updates 
 
Planning Officer Collette discussed that staff comments were submitted to consultants, and the next step is to 
review the map. 
 
Meeting adjourned at 7:14 PM. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Kayleigh Rienas 
Development Assistant 
Planning Division
